## 89ab40aedfe4

**Finding A1 — ordered curriculum is sound, arbitrary query rotation is not.** The selected sampler intentionally cycles four profiles: `canonical_anchor`, `topmost_conflict`, `stable_tie`, and `marker_only`, with four demonstrations followed by a query. On that stated ordered policy, all 192 sampled windows (64 starts × 3 bands) passed `lesson_identifiable`, all five canonical pairs matched the task's Python mirror, and all 48 crossed boundary override cases were exact. The probe covered 960 generated pairs / 800 distinct inputs at generator SHA-256 `f0808f35cb4aca9528f263bfdbba177ef76c1172e8d54dc6dc7f8df5270de27e`; see `checks/audit/89ab40aedfe4/probe.json`.

A downstream assembler that rotates any of the five pairs into the query can remove the only witness for a rival. Exact witness: easy band, seed `900000`, sample indices `0..4`; hold out pair index `2` (`stable_tie`) and use indices `0,1,3,4` as demonstrations. The `reverse_equal_population_ties` rival matches all four Racket-labeled demonstrations but differs from the Racket query at eight cells. All five inputs pass the target validator. The authoritative batch apply executed rule hash `4bc48cdc5789`; see `checks/audit/89ab40aedfe4/witness.json` and `checks/audit/89ab40aedfe4/racket.json`.

**Classification:** assembly/domain caveat, not a defect in the documented ordered production policy. No fix made. Consumers must preserve the four-profile demonstration order or expand the lesson so every allowed query rotation leaves the tie and marker-only witnesses in the demonstrations.
